name: vision_superres_bad
title: The same ESRGAN run with eight planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 2: the dirty twin of vision_superres. Its MLV402 label is the one that shows a dict of criteria silencing a high-severity pairing rule (VIS2-06), and its three MLV208 labels are the AMP protocol sub-variants the rule does not reach

expected.defect: the relativistic adversarial term is nn.BCELoss while the discriminator's last layer is an unbounded nn.Linear
expected.why: BCELoss takes log() of its input, so the first negative score produces nan and the whole run dies - or, worse, is clamped and trains on a meaningless gradient
expected.gap: the criterion is read out of a dict literal (criteria["adversarial"]), which makes the loss binding an unresolvable subscript. MLView says so in two diagnostics rather than staying silent, but the high-severity pairing is missed. One-line repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-06).

expected.defect: a bare backward() on the discriminator loss while a GradScaler is in use
expected.why: the gradients are never scaled, so under float16 they underflow to zero and the discriminator silently stops learning
expected.gap: same dict-of-scalers / untyped-loss cause as the MLV402 label above.

expected.defect: g_scaler.step() is never followed by g_scaler.update()
expected.why: the scale factor never adapts, so the first overflow freezes the generator for the rest of the run
expected.gap: the scaler arrives as scalers["g"] out of a dict literal, so the receiver does not resolve to a GradScaler.

expected.defect: clip_grad_norm_ runs on still-scaled gradients: scaler.unscale_() is gone
expected.why: max_norm=1.0 is compared against gradients multiplied by the loss scale (65536 by default), so the clip never engages and the protection is not there
expected.gap: this is the fourth documented MLV208 sub-variant and it does not fire even when the scaler IS local and resolved - see the r208a repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-07).

expected.defect: both running totals keep the live loss tensors
expected.why: the generator graph holds the RRDB trunk, the discriminator and a VGG19 slice, so retaining it for a whole epoch is an immediate out-of-memory
expected.gap: the loss is untyped for the same dict reason; MLView declares the gap in its untagged_dataflow diagnostic.

expected.why: the discriminator and the now-unfrozen VGG extractor stay in training mode for the pass that produces the reported PSNR, and the extractor's BatchNorm-free slice still accumulates a graph
expected.note: found at confidence 0.51 / possible, below mlview.minConfidence 0.6, so it never reaches the Problems panel: the generator carries no BatchNorm or Dropout, which is the architecture de-rate doing its job

expected.why: the per-image PSNR table printed each epoch lists a different set of images, so two epochs cannot be compared image by image

expected.defect: torch.load with neither map_location= nor weights_only=True
expected.why: a downloaded super-resolution checkpoint executes whatever its pickle says to execute, and a CUDA-saved checkpoint will not load on a CPU machine

expected.defect: g_optimizer.zero_grad() is gone while d_optimizer.zero_grad() remains
expected.why: every generator update applies the running sum of the epoch's gradients
expected.gap: MLV201's documented false-positive note (b) suppresses the rule when zero_grad is called on a different but resolved optimizer in a multi-optimizer set, which is exactly this shape. Recorded as `acceptable` rather than as a miss: the guard is the right trade for GAN code and the alternative is a false positive on every correct two-optimizer loop.

expected.defect: the flip and the rotation are applied to the low-resolution member of the pair only
expected.why: every augmented pair is geometrically inconsistent, so the generator is trained to un-mirror and un-rotate the image as well as to upsample it - the single most damaging bug in paired super-resolution and one that produces a loss curve that looks merely slow
expected.gap: no rule models paired augmentation. MLV114 is the nearest code (the wrong augmentation reaching the wrong place) but it is about the eval pipeline, not about pair consistency.

forbidden.why: there is no sklearn transformer in this project
the training loader is built with shuffle=True
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
both optimizers still step every batch
THE TRAP: d_scaler.step(d_optimizer) legitimately precedes the generator's backward. They are two graphs over two disjoint parameter sets, which is the documented multi-optimizer GAN guard
the only no_grad region is validate(), which contains no backward()
MultiStepLR is an epoch schedule and both schedulers are stepped in the epoch loop
clip_grad_norm_ still runs between backward() and step(); its defect is the missing unscale_, which is MLV208's, and it is labelled there
there is no softmax and no CrossEntropyLoss in this project
all three modules are moved with .to(device) and both members of every pair are moved inside the loop
seed_everything() seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda
there is no split in this project - train/ and val/ are separate directories
every nn.Module subclass calls super().__init__() first
every submodule container is nn.ModuleList or nn.Sequential

gaps.what: no rule models a frozen auxiliary network (perceptual VGG, a teacher, a frozen CLIP encoder): requires_grad_(False) plus a train() override is the protocol, and dropping either is invisible
gaps.evidence: models.py:119 against the clean twin's lines 118-122

gaps.what: no rule models paired augmentation, where one geometric decision has to be applied to every member of a tuple
gaps.evidence: data.py:79 against the clean twin's `low, high = TF.hflip(low), TF.hflip(high)`

unsupported.defect: the perceptual feature extractor is neither frozen (requires_grad_(False)) nor pinned to eval mode
unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV703 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `expected`, original note: the perceptual term back-propagates through 20 million ImageNet weights no optimizer owns - doubling the step's memory and time - and generator.train() now drags the extractor into training mode, so the distance the generator is scored on is measured by a network whose own behaviour changes between train and eval
unsupported.gap: no rule models a frozen auxiliary network. MLV703 is the nearest code in spirit (a module whose train/eval state is mishandled) but it is written for F.dropout only.
